I have resolved the `Trust anchor for certification path not found` SSL handshake error by setting up Android's Network Security Configuration for the dev CA:

1. **Copied the dev CA certificate**: Placed [`shelftap_dev_ca.pem`](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r3/work/app/src/main/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem) into `app/src/main/res/raw/`.
2. **Created Network Security Config**: Added [`network_security_config.xml`](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r3/work/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml) with a `<debug-overrides>` block trusting `@raw/shelftap_dev_ca` alongside system CAs, ensuring custom CA trust applies only to debuggable builds without compromising the production release build.
3. **Updated Manifest**: Added `android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"` to the `<application>` element in [`AndroidManifest.xml`](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r3/work/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L6-L10).
